punchline: Chicago schools on probation for low test scores showed the cheating pattern in at least 4 to 5 percent of elementary classrooms each year.
thirty_sec: In 1996 Chicago began putting schools on probation for low reading scores. Two economists then went through every student's answers on the Iowa tests from 1993 to 2000 and looked for classes whose scores jumped and then fell, with blocks of identical answers. They estimated that teachers or administrators cheated in at least 4 to 5 percent of elementary classrooms a year, mostly where many students were behind. And their method missed the careful cheaters.
